records.name: St. John the Baptist Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish in Manayunk with Sunday Masses at 9 and 11 am and 6 pm, and a weekday Mass at 7 am.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass. Once you are registered as a parishioner, you can serve in a ministry such as ushering or greeting. Adults who are curious about Catholicism can join the Tuesday evening adult class (OCIA).

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 4 pm. Sunday Masses at 9 am, 11 am and 6 pm. Weekday Mass Monday to Friday at 7 am in the chapel at 146 Rector St. Saturday confession 3 to 3:45 pm, and Sunday confession 8 to 8:45 am and 5 to 5:45 pm.

locations.label: All Saints' Chapel and Parish Center

access.notes: The church and Parish Center are wheelchair accessible, with ramps at the Rector Street entrance and the rear parking lot entrance. Van accessible spaces are in front of the school on Rector Street. The site does not say whether the restroom in the church vestibule is accessible.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass at 9 am, 11 am or 6 pm. To start the adult class, register for the session that begins Sept. 22, 2026.
first_step.basis: The adult class page welcomes adults who are only curious and explains how to sign up; Mass is open to anyone. No beginner day or orientation is listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, and the site does not say how long it runs. The adult class is a small, informal Tuesday evening group from 6:30 to 8 pm in the Parish Center, where you can ask questions about the Catholic faith. You can attend as a curious adult without joining; full attendance is required only for adults preparing to become Catholic.
first_visit_tips: Park in the church lot at the Cresson Street entrance near Pensdale, or use on-street parking on Mass days.
For the adult class, register through the parish registration page or call the office.
Call 215-482-4600 with questions. The office is open Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 4 pm, and Friday until 3 pm.

contacts.contact_name: Kristi Bushner, Adult Faith Formation Director

records.notes: The register page says new members should live inside the parish boundaries to take part regularly; Mass itself is not limited. Background checks come from the ministries page, which says anyone who serves completes the required Safe Environment checks. The volunteer page does not name Act 153 or a criminal check, so those are not recorded. The home page has an unlabeled 10/23 item, which was not used.

records.name: St. John the Evangelist Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish in Center City on South 13th Street, with Sunday Masses, a Saturday vigil, and weekday lunchtime Masses.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, on a weekday at lunchtime or on a Sunday. The parish site links to a young adult group (Jack's YACs) but does not describe what it does.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8:30 am, 10:30 am (also streamed online), 12:30 pm and 6 pm. Saturday vigil Mass at 5:15 pm. Monday to Saturday Masses at 7:45 am, 12:05 pm and 5:15 pm. Confession Wednesday to Saturday, 3:30 to 4:45 pm. Eucharistic adoration Monday to Saturday, 12:45 to 4:50 pm.

first_step.how: Drop in at a weekday lunchtime Mass or any Sunday Mass. To join the parish, fill in the online registration form on the parish website, or call the office at 215-563-4145.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to the public, and the parish has an online registration form and a phone line; no newcomer program is listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to the public. The site does not describe what a visit is like or how long Mass runs. Several Masses are offered each day, so visitors can pick a time that suits them.
first_visit_tips: Go to the church at 21 S. 13th St. for Mass. The parish office is a separate address, 1212 Ludlow St.
The online registration form has five sections and asks about your household and whether you want offering envelopes. A printable PDF is available.
The site lists no office hours or parish email address, only a contact form and the phone line.

records.notes: Phone corrected to 215-563-4145 from the parish's own pages; tier 1 had 215-563-5432 from the Archdiocese listing. Two weekday Mass times from tier 1 (8:30 am and 1:05 pm) are not on the current parish schedule and were dropped; confirm with the office. The site has no accessibility or parking page, so access is not recorded. The Organizations page returned 404. The young adult group page names only an Instagram account. The site links a Holy Redeemer Chinese CC page that was not checked.

records.name: St. Katherine of Siena Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish on Frankford Avenue in the Northeast with four Sunday Masses, starting at 6:30 am, and a Saturday vigil at 5 pm.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass. The page names a school and a religious education office but lists no public programs.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 6:30 and 8 am, 10 am and noon. Saturday vigil at 5 pm. Weekday Mass at 6:30 and 8 am, and Saturday Mass at 8 am. Confession Saturdays 4 to 4:45 pm and First Fridays 7:15 to 8 am.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass at 6:30, 8, 10 am or noon, and ask the parish about its groups at 215-637-7548.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and phone numbers are listed. The parish website could not be read, so no joining page was checked.

records.notes: The parish website failed on two tries with a TLS handshake error, so nothing beyond the tier 1 sources was read. Re-run this record when the site is reachable, and check its joining, religious education and events pages first.

records.name: St. Malachy Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish near 11th and Master Streets with a Sunday Mass at 10 am, a weekday lunchtime Mass at the Temple University Newman Center, and a food pantry.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Sunday 10 am Mass or the weekday lunchtime Mass at the Newman Center. The St. Malachy Food Pantry at 1429 N. 11th St. is named on the Archdiocese July 3, 2026 day of service list, with no hours or eligibility shown.

schedule.text: Sunday Mass at 10 am. Saturday Mass at 9 am from September to May. Weekday Mass Monday to Friday at 12:10 pm at the Temple University Newman Center, 2129 N. Broad St. Sunday confession 9 to 9:45 am. Weekday confession 11 am to noon at the Newman Center.

first_step.how: Come to the Sunday 10 am Mass at the church on 11th St. above Master St., or to the weekday 12:10 pm Mass at the Newman Center. Call the rectory at 215-763-1305 about parish groups.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and the rectory phone is listed; the parish website is blocked, so no joining page could be read.
first_visit_tips: Weekday Mass is at the Temple University Newman Center on Broad Street, while Sunday Mass is at the church on 11th Street above Master Street.
Confession is offered before Sunday Mass and on weekdays at the Newman Center, per the Archdiocese page.

records.notes: The parish website returned a 403 on the home page, so nothing from the parish's own site was read. The food pantry is named only on the Archdiocese day of service list, with no hours or eligibility. One web search found no listing for a St. Malachy pantry at 1429 N. 11th St., so treat the pantry as unverified and call the rectory before sending anyone. The Archdiocese page gives 1429 N. 11th St. as the rectory address. Independence Mission School appears on the same page as the school students attend; it is listed as a lead, not a parish school.

records.name: Saint Mark's Church
records.summary: An Episcopal parish on Locust Street that serves a Saturday meal called the Soup Bowl to about 140 guests each week. It also runs a food cupboard and a choir with public concerts, and holds a Newcomer Brunch.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Saturday Soup Bowl (6 to 8 am), sit in on a Sunday service, or attend the Newcomer Brunch. Volunteers help make the soup, set tables, serve, and clean up.

schedule.text: Saturday Soup Bowl from 6 to 8 am. Saturday Low Mass at 10 am. Sunday: 8 am Low Mass, 9 am Family Mass, 10 am Christian Formation (September to June), and 11 am Choral High Mass. Choral Evensong and Benediction at 4 pm on the first Sunday of the month, October to June. Monday to Friday: 9 am Morning Prayer, 12:10 pm Low Mass, and 5:30 pm Evening Prayer.

first_step.how: Come to the Newcomer Brunch on Sunday, October 11 at 12:30 pm, or sit in on any Sunday service. Call 215-735-1416 with questions.
first_step.basis: The home page lists a Newcomer Brunch, and Sunday services are open to visitors; the membership page explains how to join but lists no newcomer classes.
first_step.what_to_expect: The parish says its church is for all people. Communion is normally for people who are baptized, and others can ask for a blessing at the altar rail instead. Coffee and snacks come after the 9 and 11 am services, a good place to meet people. The site does not say how long services last or what they cost.
first_visit_tips: On Sundays you may park on the side of the street that is normally off limits if you display an Attending Saint Mark's permit. Ushers hand them out, and they also sit on shelves just inside the main doors.
The FAQ says the church is near several public transit options, but the site does not name the lines or stops.
The site does not explain the Soup Bowl guest rules, so call 215-735-1416 before you come if you want to know them.

records.notes: The Getting Here page returned a 404, so transit and parking come only from the FAQ. The Soup Bowl volunteer contact on the site is a personal email address; it is left out, and the office phone is recorded instead. The Soup Bowl page gives its guest hours as 6 to 8 am, which tier 1 did not have. Its soup calendar has some dates out of order and was not used. The October events on the home page have no year written, so they were not used as sign of life; the last sign of life is kept from tier 1.

records.name: St. Martha Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish on Academy Road in the Northeast with three Sunday Masses, daily morning Mass, and a parish school.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, meet with the parish after Sunday Mass to register, or ask about children's religious education (PREP) or adult faith formation (RCIA).

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8 am, 10 am and noon. Saturday vigil Mass at 4 pm. Weekday and Saturday Mass at 8:15 am. Holy Day Masses at 8:15 am, noon and 7 pm. Saturday confession 2:30 to 3:30 pm. Religious education (PREP) runs Sunday mornings from 8 to 9:45 am during the school year.

cost.text: Mass is free to attend. Children's religious education (PREP) has a yearly registration fee per child: $125 for one child, $100 each for two, and $90 each for three or more (2025 to 2026 rates).

first_step.how: Come to any Sunday Mass, including the Saturday 4 pm vigil, then meet with the parish after Mass to register.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says staff meet people after any Sunday Mass to register, and Mass is open to anyone; no newcomer program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Registration is a meeting with the parish after Mass, which is how new parishioners start. The site does not describe a typical Sunday visit, how long Mass runs, or what to wear. Children must be registered before the first day of religious education class, and the site says children are not registered on the first day.
first_visit_tips: The rectory is open Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 4 pm, and Friday, 9 am to 1 pm. It is closed on weekends; the FAQ says Saturdays are by appointment, which the footer does not match.
Register children for PREP before the first class, since the site says no child is registered on the first day.

records.notes: The religious education page and its key dates cover the 2025 to 2026 school year. The newest dated item is the April 24 to 25, 2026 First Communion, so last sign of life is 2026-04; no 2026 to 2027 dates are posted. Cost level is set to low because of the PREP fees; Mass is free. The site lists two different numbers and two personal email addresses for one religious education staff member, so only the rectory number is recorded. The RCIA page points to another staff member's phone, not recorded here; the parish office can connect people. The address is 11301 Academy Road on the parish's own pages, replacing 11321 from tier 1. The Organizations page returned 404, so parish groups are not described. The Pre-Jordan baptism class is named without detail.

records.name: St. Martin de Porres Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 24th and Lehigh Avenue in North Philadelphia with a Sunday Mass at 10 am and weekday morning Mass.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Sunday 10 am Mass or a weekday morning Mass. The Archdiocese page lists no community programs.

schedule.text: Sunday Mass at 10 am. Weekday Mass at 7 am, or 8 am in summer. Sunday confession at 9:30 am, and by appointment.

first_step.how: Come to the Sunday 10 am Mass, or call the rectory at 215-228-8330 to ask about parish groups.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and the rectory phone is listed; the parish website returned a 403 error, so no joining page could be checked.

records.notes: The parish website returned a 403 on the home page; it was not retried, so no deeper detail is available. The record is carried over from tier 1, with the first step as best supported.
